conviction_note: Two measurements that differ in size on purpose. The findings sum to +2.3, carried mainly by the Oct 29 8-K, which says Walmart's new commitment 'could increase Symbotic's future backlog by an amount up to $6.92B' (about +31% on a backlog that has sat at $22.3-22.7B for a year) while the stock now trades below its pre-announcement price. The scaled number is only +0.3, abs 15 x p_up 51. Three things pull p_up to a coin flip: (1) SYM has sold its prints (down after the last three, 3 of 7 up in the baseline history); (2) the CFO pointed to soft near-term trajectory signals (Q4 starts 'a little short' of Q3, opex rising 'in the quarters to come', gross margin stabilising rather than expanding, the next-gen inflection only in 2H of next year); (3) the 25-delta skew is +8.7 toward puts. The search was cut by a budget limit, so the hunt is marked unfinished.

findings.finding: Symbotic's Oct 29 8-K (Item 1.01, Enterprise Master Automation Agreement with Walmart) describes Walmart's new commitment of about $6B of systems purchases plus a $125M development-program addendum. The filing calls it 'in addition to the purchase commitments under the Existing Program Agreements' and says it 'may not be reduced without the mutual written consent' of both parties. It also states that it 'could increase Symbotic's future backlog by an amount up to $6,920,000,000'. That is about +31% on the $22.5B Q3 backlog, which has sat between $22.3B and $22.7B for a year. The FQ4 print and call are the first time management can say how much of this enters backlog and on what conversion timing. The preview's stated bar is 'backlog growth'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog and outlook have driven this name's big prints. Nov 2025 FQ4 rose +39.4% (baseline) and Aug 2026 fell -14.9% when the SymMicro rollout slipped to 2028 (Simply Wall St summary). The announcement itself drew only +1.9% premarket on Oct 30 ($38.10, https://www.rttnews.com/3706213/symbotic-expands-walmart-automation-deal-with-6-bln-initial-spending-commitment.aspx). The stock then fell to a $31.10 low.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public, but the price shows no credit for it. Spot is $36.33 against $37.93 on Oct 30 and about $37.4 before the release. The stock made new lows after the announcement, and the Nov 15 Earnings Whispers preview does not mention the backlog effect and lists backlog as 'flat for a year'. If the market had priced a +31% backlog step, the stock would sit above its pre-deal level and the skew would not be +8.7 toward puts. The caveat: the Q4 backlog date (Sept 27) comes before the Oct 29 signing, so the reported backlog may not show the addition, and the market may already treat the $6B as multi-year Walmart spend it expected anyway.
findings.independence: The trade press covering the release (https://www.supplychaindive.com/press-release/20261030-walmart-and-symbotic-expand-commercial-agreement-to-support-supply-chain-tr/) confirms the scope: 25 RDCs, BreakPack and SymMicro. It is the same announcement, so it is not independent evidence for the backlog number. Only the 8-K carries the $6.92B figure.

findings.finding: The Q4 revenue bar sits inside the company's own raised guide. The guide is $760-780M (raised from $700-720M); consensus is about $774M, two agreeing sources. In Q3, revenue was $721M (+22% y/y, +7% q/q) and adj. EBITDA was $95M against an $80-85M guide, so the company has been landing at or above the top of its ranges. A print of about $775-780M is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold. Q3 FY26 beat revenue and EBITDA and the stock fell -14.9% on the guide and the SymMicro delay. Q2 FY26 fell -7.7% and Q1 FY26 rose +0.6% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. Consensus is already at $774M, the upper half of the guide. Only a print above $780M or a clear EBITDA beat would be news, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-15 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/SYM/23213): consensus $773.9M and whisper equal to consensus, so there is no hidden bar.

findings.finding: On the Q3 call management signalled a soft near-term trajectory. Q4 system starts would be 'maybe just a little short of' Q3's 11. Opex will see 'a little bit of an uptick... not only in the fourth quarter but in the quarters to come'. Gross margin should 'stabilise' at about 25% rather than expand. 'The real inflection point of the next generation storage structure will really happen in the second half of next year.' The 400-store SymMicro order runs 'probably until early 28', and micro-fulfillment revenue is high-single-digit millions a quarter. Against Q1 FY27 consensus of about $817.5M (+6% q/q off the Q4 midpoint, one possibly stale source), a cautious Q1 guide is the main downside path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide and rollout-timing disappointments produced -14.9% (Aug 2026), -7.7% (May 2026), -13.8% (Aug 2025) and -15.9% (Feb 2025) in the baseline. A constructive outlook produced +39.4% (Nov 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is down about 20% since the Aug print and the skew is +8.7. The specific Q1 FY27 bar ($817.5M) comes from one possibly stale table, and nobody has reconciled it with the CFO's 'steady' framing and fewer starts. If the market had fully priced a flat or soft Q1 guide, the consensus would sit nearer $790-800M.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://earningswhispers.com/article/SYM/23213) independently notes the SymMicro slip to early 2028 and flat backlog. The quotes come from the call transcript, which shares its source with the Q3 release in finding 2 but not the same line. The SymMicro delay is merged here rather than filed separately because it rests on the same transcript and was the stated cause of the August drop.

findings.finding: Short interest was 17.54M shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, 10.2 days to cover, up from 15.77M on 2026-08-14. Disputed float estimates run from about 14% to 40%. That is a crowded short into a print where the reaction history includes +39.4% (Nov 2025), so a squeeze adds an upside mechanism on any positive outlook or backlog surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +39.36% move on 2025-11-24 (baseline) came on the same fiscal-Q4 print with a large short base.
findings.why_not_priced: The short is visible, but the skew (+8.7 toward puts) and the IV show the market paying for downside, not for squeeze risk. A squeeze priced into the options would show as call-side skew.
findings.independence: Benzinga short-interest page (undated, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SYM/short-interest), 31.7-40.5% of float. It is a different source but stale.

findings.finding: The counterparty that is about 85% of revenue reported strength after Symbotic last spoke. On Nov 19 Walmart raised its FY27 adj. EPS outlook for the second time to $2.84-2.89, with US e-commerce +23% and store deliveries +40%. That supports continued automation spend, but Walmart's call did not address DC automation or Symbotic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of SYM reacting to Walmart's results specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy. Walmart's strength is public, and it moves SYM only through capex appetite, which the Oct 29 commitment already locks in. The size is small for that reason.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Same direction as the Oct 29 commitment in finding 1, which is the direct evidence.

findings.finding: Insider selling into the print is small and pre-planned. Director Todd Krasnow sold 2,000 shares at $37.2-40.1 on 2026-11-02 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-12-08. Officer Michael Dunn has sold about 1,165-1,513 shares every two weeks under a plan adopted 2025-06-12, most recently 1,286 shares around 2026-11-18. A cluster of Form 144s on Oct 26-28 matches RSU vesting.
findings.why_not_priced: It carries no information. Routine plan sales of a few tens of thousands of dollars are not a signal.
findings.independence: Form 144, 2026-11-18 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1837240/000195004726011296/xsl144X01/primary_doc.xml): Dunn's sale history, all labelled 10b5-1 except one sale on 08/24.

findings.finding: September sell-side cuts set a lower sentiment bar into the print. Needham cut its target from $75 to $60 (Buy) on 2026-09-15 and Barclays cut from $44 to $38 (Underweight) on 2026-09-08. MarketBeat's tally is 7 Buy, 4 Hold and 4 Sell, with consensus at 'Hold'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell about 6% on 2026-09-18 after the Needham cut, with no company news (TickerSpark/AAII summaries).
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. The cuts were two months ago and the stock has fallen since.
findings.independence: Needham's cut is reported by Benzinga via a MarketBeat aggregator (https://www.themarketsdaily.com/?p=9939998).

outside_window.finding: The SymMicro 400-store order runs to 'probably early 28'. The next-generation storage structure inflects in 2H of next year. GreenBox Lathrop was expected live 60-90 days after Aug 5. All of these are operational milestones dated beyond the window, unless the call updates them.

baseline_tension: The main finding (backlog up to +$6.92B, with the stock below its pre-announcement price) cuts against the +8.7 put skew and the -4% 20-day run-up. The guidance-trajectory finding agrees with them. Net, the evidence pulls against the skew only mildly, so p_up sits at 51 rather than leaning long.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells its beats, down on the last 3 prints): backlog finding cut from +2.5 to +2.0 and the in-guide revenue finding from +0.5 to +0.2.
Lesson 7 (crowded short, about 10 days to cover): guidance-trajectory negative cut from -1.5 to -1.2. The sign against the +8.7 skew is moved to p_up 51 from 52.
Lesson 6 (bar verified): consensus confirmed by two agreeing sources plus the company guide, so no cap. Q1 FY27 consensus has a single source, so the guidance finding stays small.
Lessons 5 and 9: the Walmart proxy finding was left small at +0.3. Lessons 2 and 4 do not apply (no one-off, no financing).
